facts.content: Patient presents with a 3-day headache that is global with right peri-orbital predominance.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day HA, global w/ R peri-orbital predominance

facts.content: The headache pain is constant with flares and rated 8 out of 10 in severity.
The headache had a gradual onset at work and was worse the next morning.
facts.source_text: gradual onset at work; worse next morning

facts.content: The headache is associated with photophobia.
At onset of the headache, the patient experienced visual phenomena described as shooting lights.
The headache is associated with nausea without vomiting.
The patient reports no vision loss or blurring.
The patient reports no neck pain or stiffness.
The patient denies speech difficulty.
The patient reports no focal weakness.
The patient reports no head injury.
The patient reports no fevers.
The patient reports no rash.
The headache has impacted concentration.
Due to the headache, the patient has missed work.
The patient reduced screen brightness because of the headache.
The patient reports that prior headaches were usually relieved by ibuprofen but not this episode.
facts.source_text: Prior HAs usually relieved by ibuprofen; not this episode

facts.content: The patient reports no past medical or surgical history.
The patient takes no regular medications.
The patient self-treated with ibuprofen three times a day for two days without effect.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's mother has migraines that are worse with season change.
The patient's sister has infrequent migraines.
The patient lives with three housemates.
The patient works in IT with computer use.
The patient wears glasses.
The patient has not had a recent eye exam.
The patient reports mild to moderate stress related to a new project.
The patient is a social smoker.
The patient drinks alcohol and not only socially.
Assessment is probable migraine with photophobia with or without visual aura lasting three days at 8 out of 10 severity.
facts.source_text: 1) Probable migraine w/ photophobia ± visual aura, 3 days, 8/10

facts.content: The migraine is refractory to suboptimal NSAID dosing.
No red flags are noted, including no fever, meningismus, neurologic deficits, or trauma.
facts.source_text: no red flags (no fever, meningismus, neuro deficits, trauma)

facts.content: Plan includes optimizing NSAID dosing with ibuprofen up to two tablets three times daily or switching to naproxen.
facts.source_text: Analgesia: optimize NSAID dosing (ibuprofen up to 2 tabs TID) or switch to naproxen

facts.content: Plan includes adding paracetamol for analgesia.
Codeine is prescribed today.
Patient is advised to keep a headache diary and identify potential triggers.
facts.source_text: Self-care: HA diary; identify potential triggers

facts.content: An eye test is recommended if the patient experiences eyestrain.
facts.source_text: Vision/ergonomics: recommend eye test if eyestrain

facts.content: Patient is advised to return to clinic in 1 to 2 weeks, or earlier if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
facts.source_text: FU: RTC 1–2 wks; earlier if worsening or not improving

facts.content: Safety net advice is given for urgent review if new or worsening visual changes, focal weakness, or systemic illness occur.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: urgent review for new/worsening visual changes, focal weakness, or if systemically unwell
